claims.claim: The paper reports that more speakers help more than more hours per speaker, while accent-diversity gains are minimal under controlled speaker count.
claims.limitations: Languages, accent labels, low-resource budgets, model/training choices, and zero-shot evaluation bound transfer; this is not a universal data-collection law.

claims.claim: The paper reports similar difficulty characteristics for humans and ASR and no WER effect from filler presence alone.
claims.limitations: 54 listeners, nine systems, utterance design, languages, and WER/recall definitions bound transfer; matched error patterns do not establish cognitive equivalence.

claims.claim: The paper reports better reproducibility with low-noise-floor RIRs in highly reverberant rooms and at 5 m, while truncation usually did not help.
claims.limitations: Rooms, source distances, RIR measurement, listening protocol, and speech-in-noise task bound transfer; perceptual reproducibility is not exact physical localization.

claims.claim: The paper reports average and per-child gains for both model types, with remaining limitations on non-linguistic child speech.
claims.limitations: Child corpus, adaptation methods, update stability, model family, and evaluation conditions bound transfer; average WER gains are not proof of safe continual deployment.

claims.claim: The paper reports high speech quality at 1.2 kbps and lower complexity than compared end-to-end codecs.
claims.limitations: Datasets, bitrate, codec baselines, quality metrics, hardware, and real-time implementation bound transfer; reported quality is not proof for every channel or listener.

claims.claim: The paper reports retraining-free contextual recognition improvements using WCTC-Biasing.
claims.limitations: Keyword lists, wildcard design, domains, decoder thresholds, and test distributions bound transfer; contextual gains do not guarantee lower errors on arbitrary speech.

claims.claim: The paper reports improved robust long-form recognition from inference-time positional alignment.
claims.limitations: Model, long-form segmentation, positional formulation, decoding settings, and evaluation corpora bound transfer; reported robustness is not universal streaming reliability.

claims.claim: The paper reports unified microphone conversion results across device mappings without paired examples for every target pair.
claims.limitations: Device inventory, pairing protocol, training coverage, content preservation metrics, and acoustic conditions bound transfer; channel conversion is not the same as recognizer invariance.
